title: Cap. VI Arg. 2: from the nature of special liberating grace — Augustine
latin: Secundum argumentum desumetur a natura gratiae specialis liberantis, et de facto salutiferae. Nam ut recte observavit Augustinus, Praedestinatio non est gratiae cujuscunque, sed talis gratiae praeparatio: et talis gratia, nempe de facto salutifera, est praedestinationis effectus. Si igitur haec gratia in cordibus electorum fidem gignit, non invenit, tum multo magis ipsa electio, quae dandae talis gratiae causa fuit, pure gratuita esse debet, et ex nullo humanae voluntatis actu praeeunte, sed solummodo ex Divino beneplacito, pendere.
pass_a: The second argument will be taken from the nature of special liberating grace, and of that which is in fact saving. For as Augustine rightly observed, Predestination is not the preparation of just any grace, but of such grace: and such grace, namely that which is in fact saving, is the effect of predestination. If therefore this grace in the hearts of the elect begets faith, does not find it, then much more election itself, which was the cause of such grace to be given, ought to be purely free, and to depend on no preceding act of the human will, but only on the Divine good pleasure.
pass_b: Second argument: from the nature of special liberating grace — grace that is in fact saving. As Augustine rightly observed, Predestination is not preparation of just any grace, but of such grace; and such grace, namely that which is in fact saving, is predestination's effect. If this grace in the elects' hearts begets faith rather than finds it, then much more election itself, the cause of giving such grace, must be purely free — depending on no preceding act of the human will, but only on the divine good pleasure.

lemmas.gloss: begets faith, does not find it

title: Cap. VI Arg. 2: 2 Tim. 1:9; Prosper — this grace barred by no evil merits, bought by no good
latin: Sic loquitur Apostolus, Servavit nos, et vocavit vocatione sancta, non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito et gratia. 2 Tim. i. 9. Haec gratia nullis malis meritis arcetur, nullis bonis impetratur, Prosper, ad Cap. Gallor. resp. 8. Haec gratia facit ut velimus, facit ut faciamus, facit ut credamus. Haec gratia bonas voluntates in hominibus operatur, Augustinus, De grat. Christi, cap. 29.
pass_a: Thus speaks the Apostle, He has saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not from our works, but from his purpose and grace. 2 Tim. 1:9. This grace is barred by no evil merits, is obtained by no good ones, Prosper, Response to the Chapters of the Gauls, 8. This grace makes that we will, makes that we do, makes that we believe. This grace works good wills in men, Augustine, On the Grace of Christ, chapter 29.
pass_b: So Paul: he saved us and called us with a holy calling — not from our works, but from his purpose and grace (2 Tim. 1:9). Prosper (Response to the Gallican Chapters, 8): no evil merits bar this grace, no good ones purchase it. Augustine (On the Grace of Christ, ch. 29): it makes us will, makes us act, makes us believe, and works good wills in men.

lemmas.gloss: not from works but purpose and grace

title: Cap. VI Arg. 2: De bono persever. — this grace prevents faith, will, and all our obedience
latin: Uno verbo, ut optime Augustinus, De bono persever. cap. 15. Haec gratia praevenit fidem, praevenit voluntatem, praevenit omnem obedientiam nostram; et haec omnia in eo cui datur, et cui haec omnia praevenit, operatur. Hisce omnibus ego addo, quod adversarii inficias ire non audebunt, talem gratiam dari a Deo ea intentione, ut haec omnia in electis et secundum propositum vocatis producat.
pass_a: In a word, as Augustine best, On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 15. This grace prevents faith, prevents the will, prevents all our obedience; and works all these in him to whom it is given, and whom it prevents in all these. To all these I add what the adversaries will not dare to deny, that such grace is given by God with that intention, that it may produce all these things in the elect and those called according to purpose.
pass_b: In a word, as Augustine best puts it (On the Gift of Perseverance, ch. 15): this grace goes before faith, before the will, before all our obedience — and works all these in the one to whom it is given and whom it thus goes before. Add what adversaries will not dare deny: God gives such grace with the intention that it produce all these in the elect and those called according to purpose.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 2 close: faith-bearing grace given by freest will — so predestination unbound to prior free-choice acts
latin: Quandoquidem igitur haec specialis et efficax gratia quae fidem parit, et conversionem, non praerequirit antecedaneam fidei nostrae conditionem, sed datur quibusdam, aliis non datur, pro liberrima dantis aut non-dantis voluntate; manifestum est ipsam praedestinationem, quae est causa talis gratiae praeparatae et donatae, non esse alligatam actibus ullis antecedaneis humani arbitrii, sed constitutam in gratuito beneplacito ipsius Dei, juxta illud Apostoli, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
pass_a: Since therefore this special and efficacious grace which brings forth faith, and conversion, does not prerequire an antecedent condition of our faith, but is given to certain ones, not given to others, according to the freest will of the one giving or not-giving; it is plain that predestination itself, which is the cause of such grace prepared and gifted, is not bound to any antecedent acts of human choice, but is constituted in the free good pleasure of God himself, according to that of the Apostle, I will have mercy on whom I will have had mercy, Rom. 9:15.
pass_b: So this special efficacious grace that brings forth faith and conversion does not prerequire an antecedent condition of our faith — it is given to some and not to others by the freest will of the Giver. Plainly then predestination itself, the cause of such grace prepared and gifted, is not bound to any antecedent acts of human choice, but is constituted in God's free good pleasure — per Rom. 9:15, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.

lemmas.gloss: I will have mercy on whom I will
